Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.gametest

Class PickerExportGameTestsLogic

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.gametest.PickerExportGameTestsLogic
public final class PickerExportGameTestsLogic extends Object
The server-side export validation (PickerExportService) and the canonical JSON it emits. Only the rejection paths of the service are exercised — they return before any file is written, so nothing touches the test world's datapacks and no /reload fires mid-run (the success path, and with it the 10-second cooldown, is covered by manual verification against a real server). Each test uses a fresh player id so the all-attempt throttle remains independent.

  • Method Details

    • exportRejectsUnknownEntityType

      public static void exportRejectsUnknownEntityType(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Export refuses an entity type the server does not know. No in-game form with an unmodified client, which exports only mobs that exist; guards the server against a forged export packet.

    • exportRejectsEnderDragon

      public static void exportRejectsEnderDragon(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Export refuses the ender dragon. In game: as a creative operator, summon an ender dragon, choose it in the picker with V, create an eye with /sg create 0 0 0, and run /sg export; the export is refused with a message and nothing is written.

    • exportPacketRefusesOversizedConfig

      public static void exportPacketRefusesOversizedConfig(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The client's pre-send size check. In game: author a mob with a very large number of eyes in the picker and run /sg export; the client answers "too large to send" instead of the server disconnecting you, while an ordinary config exports normally.

    • exportRejectsGarbageTypedField

      public static void exportRejectsGarbageTypedField(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      RuntimeConfig.CODEC's fields are required, so a wrong-typed field is a decode failure rather than something DFU swallows into a default, and the service refuses the payload as malformed. No in-game form with an unmodified client; guards the server against a forged export packet.

    • exportRejectsEmptyPayloadAsMalformed

      public static void exportRejectsEmptyPayloadAsMalformed(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      An empty compound is missing required fields, so it never reaches the usable-eyes check. No in-game form with an unmodified client; guards the server against a forged export packet.

    • exportRejectsConfigWithNoUsableEyes

      public static void exportRejectsConfigWithNoUsableEyes(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A well-formed config that simply carries no eyes is refused by the usable-eyes check. In game: choose a mob in the picker, delete every eye with /sg delete, and run /sg export; the export is refused because there are no eyes to draw.

    • exportRejectsUnsafeNumericConfig

      public static void exportRejectsUnsafeNumericConfig(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Export refuses geometry outside the validator's limits, such as a non-finite position. No in-game form, since picker commands accept only finite numbers; guards the server against a forged export packet.

    • canonicalJsonWritesDefaultValuedFields

      public static void canonicalJsonWritesDefaultValuedFields(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The written form pins values that equal their defaults rather than eliding them, so a file's meaning can't drift with the code. crossTarget sits at its default in most real configs, so it's the field checked by name here; that no field is dropped at all is guarded by the value round-trip in SerializationGameTests. In game: run /sg exportall and open any exported JSON; every eye lists "crossTarget", including -1.
